arguments.value: Mutual Insurance Corporation of America (MICOA), a Michigan insurance corporation, and Stratton, Cheeseman & Walsh-Nevada, Inc., a Nevada corporation, entered into this agency agreement. The agreement gives the agency authority to solicit health care liability and professional liability insurance in Nevada, issue certificates and binders only under MICOA’s rules and only when authorized, service policies, report claims and lawsuits promptly, and operate as MICOA’s exclusive Nevada agent for the listed professional liability products unless MICOA declines a submitted risk. In return, MICOA pays commissions on covered business, shares some approved promotional costs, and allows the agency to request subagency appointments only with MICOA’s written approval. The agency must maintain required errors-and-omissions and fidelity/electronic crime insurance, and both parties must follow MICOA underwriting and approval requirements. If the agreement ends, MICOA must buy the agency’s expirations for the business produced under the agreement, subject to stated exclusions for subagency business, and the agency is then barred for two years from selling to those Nevada MICOA insureds. Either party may terminate on 120 days’ written notice, and the agreement also ends immediately for certain misconduct or if the agency loses its license. The agreement does not state a fixed term; it remains in effect until terminated under its terms or as required by law.
